newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KLINSMANN AT CENTRE OF TOTTENHAM DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLINSMANN AT CENTRE OF TOTTENHAM DISPUTE.

text.p: A team doctor at English soccer club Tottenham claimed on Wednesday that he lost his job for trying to stop German international striker Juergen Klinsmann from playing after a serious head injury.
Doctor Patrick Keating told an industrial tribunal that he lost his standing at the premier league club because he refused to bend the rules on safety in the interests of club profits.
"I was constructively dismissed precisely because I was not prepared to bend the rules and compromise the health of players at the club," he told the London tribunal.

Keating said his relationship with Tottenham chairman Alan Sugar and former Argentine manager Ossie Ardiles deteriorated after Klinsmann was injured in a clash of heads during a league match against Sheffield Wednesday in August 1994.

He told the tribunal that Klinsmann showed signs of having an epileptic fit and he recommended that the striker should not play again until he had seen a neurological expert who could give the all-clear. He alleged that Sugar and club physiotherapist Tony Lenaghan ignored his advice.
"They told me that he would be referred to a neurosurgeon of his choice but would not give me the neurosurgeon's name," Keating said.
"I expressed my disquiet to the club physiotherapist about the unacceptable delay in assessing a potentially serious head injury which could have injured his life.
"He told me that the club were very angry with me and that I was to keep a low profile. He told me that I was very naive about the politics and the economics of the situation.
"He said that Alan Sugar and (chief executive) Claude Littner were only concerned about the share price and that the health and safety of players was not their main priority."
Tottenham denies unfair dismissal. In a written statement read out to the tribunal, Lenaghan denied the allegations.
"It is ludicrous to suggest that it is in the interests of the club that health is less important than money," he said.
The doctor eventually resigned in May last year after management swapped him and his deputy around.
Klinsmann, the German national team captain, played one season at Tottenham before returning to Germany with Bayern Munich in 1995. He has recently joined Italian club Sampdoria.
